title: Bootstrapper mini-flows and prompt-sanity notebook
body:
Status: draft - lightweight notes + working checklist for a 15-minute bootstrapper flow aimed at new engineers trying the Redwood SDK for the first time. Purpose: give a super-fast, low-friction path to a meaningful sample (local dev loop + one end-to-end request + minimal telemetry) and a set of prompt-sanity checks to catch common mistakes before sending heavy traffic to hosted or dedicated endpoints.

Context / motivation:
- Many onboarding docs are too long and expect users to read sections they won't. We need a bite-sized flow that finishes in ~15 minutes and provides a deterministic success signal (sample app responds with expected JSON and telemetry shows a successful token usage event).
- Focus on ensuring prompt/response shape, token budgeting, and fallback routing are visible to the dev.
- Works for hosted API and local mock runner.

Target persona: backend/frontend engineer, familiar with CLI and Node/Python, wants to validate an LLM integration quickly.

Success criteria (what to validate at the end):
1) Sample app starts in local mode in <90s.
2) First request returns expected structured JSON (name, intent, confidence) and logs include model name + token estimate.
3) SDK telemetry captures a "bootstrap-first-request" event.
4) A prompt-sanity check warns if prompt > recommended token budget or contains unescaped JSON that would break structured output parsing.

Mini-flow (steps):
1) Pre-reqs: git clone repo; node 18+ or python3.10; REDWOOD_API_KEY in env (or --local-mode flag).
2) Install: yarn install | pip install -r requirements.txt (two-commands max).
3) Run local dev server: 
   - node ./examples/bootstrapper/server.js --local-mode (exposes http://localhost:3000/sample)
   - OR python examples/bootstrapper/server.py --local-mode
4) Smoke request (curl):
   curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/sample -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"Classify intent: 'book-flight' for text: \"I need to go to SFO tomorrow\"","budget_tokens":150}'
5) Expected JSON response:
   {"intent":"book_flight","entities":{"dest":"SFO"},"confidence":0.91}
6) Quick checks: server logs should print:
   - "model: redwood-autogen-v1 (hosted)" or "local-runner"
   - "token_estimate: 120"
   - "telemetry_event: bootstrap-first-request"
7) Prompt-sanity warnings (printed client-side before call):
   - If prompt length > 800 chars -> "prompt too long for default 150-token budget"
   - If prompt contains unescaped JSON-looking text -> "possible malformed structured-output input; consider escaping or using system message"

Engineering notes / implementation details:
- Add a tiny validator module (prompt_sanity.js / prompt_sanity.py) that runs during SDK client prepareRequest and returns a list of warnings. Warnings should be non-blocking but surfaced in console and in telemetry under event:prompt-sanity-warning.
- The sample server should instrument a minimal telemetry event to internal dev analytics: name, model_variant, token_estimate, warnings[]. This can be toggled off for privacy.
- Provide two transport modes in the sample: hosted API (reads REDWOOD_API_KEY) and local mock runner (--local-mode). Local mock runner will simulate a model response and mimic token counts.

CLI snippets to include in quickstart README (copy-pastable):
- Set env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
- Start: node examples/bootstrapper/server.js --local-mode
- Test: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/sample -d '{"prompt":"...","budget_tokens":100}'

Failure modes and debugging tips (short):
- Response is HTML or 502: check local-mode flag and proxy settings. If hosted, check API key and network egress.
- Wrong JSON shape: run with --dump-response to show raw LLM output; check for missing system message that enforces structured output.
- Token budget exceeded: warn and show token_estimate in logs; offer quick quantization suggestion (e.g., shorten context, switch to compact model).

Telemetry and privacy considerations:
- Telemetry event "bootstrap-first-request" should not include PII or full prompt. Only include token_estimate, model_variant, region, and whether prompt_sanity warnings fired.
- Provide clear opt-out: env REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0 disables instrumentation.

Next steps / TODOs (short backlog):
- [ ] Draft short README.md with the 15-minute flow and CLI snippets. (Aisha)
- [ ] Implement prompt_sanity module for JS + Py and unit tests for common trap cases (unescaped JSON, excessively long prompt). (Liam)
- [ ] Add telemetry event mapping + server-side debug route to fetch last 10 dev telemetry events. (Devon)
- [ ] Create a tiny e2e smoke test in CI that runs the local-mode sample and asserts expected JSON. (Sofia)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How opinionated should the prompt-sanity rules be? Start conservative: length, unescaped-json, forbidden control chars. Expand based on adoption.
- Should we require structured-output schema enforcement in the sample? Prefer showing both: permissive run and an enforced run (flag --strict-schema).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally compact; aim is to iterate quickly and ship a single-file example that teams can embed in their repos. Keep the API surface minimal and the failure modes easy to understand.

Handy references for implementers:
- Confluence:DEVPATH-312 (design notes for quickstart telemetry)
- Jira: RX-1284 (bootstrapper sample work ticket)
- GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-bootstrapper/pull/47 (in-progress sample)

-- end notebook (rough)
